The book's entry preserves the consensus primary referent (innumerable multitude) but materially refines its extension by explicitly linking it to the unstable-foundation image. The multitude is not merely a quantity but the very substance of the shifting foundation; building on sand therefore means building on the crowd rather than the covenant-rock. This is a tighter causal connection than the consensus treats the two as independent alternatives.

The book adds the interpretive claim that the multitude itself constitutes the unstable foundation (the crowd vs covenant-rock), narrowing the parable's application to a crowd-based worldview. It excludes the consensus's broader unstable foundation sense (hearing without doing, general lack of obedience) and reclassifies it as specifically crowd-based rather than teaching-based.

The printed citations provide strong support, covering both the multitude passages and the foundation parable.
